transcript.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Our invoice for Org copperleaf-ai lists 'Embeddings, Aug 3-9' twice. Last time support said duplicates can’t be credited here and have to go through Finance, but could you credit the duplicate?

{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Goal: decide from console evidence and current policy what Support may do about a charge, do it with approval, and tell the developer.

1. Gather. If the developer has not given them, call `ask_developer` once for the org (or account id), the invoice id or month, and the lines/amounts in question; add request ids if they say specific requests were mis-billed.
2. Read, in one round: `account_overview` (org or account id) and `search_knowledge` for the policy on this kind of request (e.g. "duplicate charge credit Support limit", "what Support may credit charter", "refund request billed in error", "goodwill credit request", "SLA credit request contract"). Then `invoice_details` for the invoice. If the developer gave only a month, pick the invoice whose period covers it (periods follow the account's billing timezone where policy says so).
3. Check the billing channel first. If the account is billed by a marketplace or reseller, Support does not credit or dispute that invoice: find the policy for that channel and tell the developer who handles it.
4. Classify with console evidence only:
   - Duplicate: `console_confirmed_duplicates` lists the lines (same request ids on the same invoice) and names the original (the line the usage records point to) and the copy. Only the copy is ever credited or disputed. If no single original is identified, treat it as an unconfirmed duplicate. Same description or amount alone is not a duplicate; lines in `lookalike_lines` bill different requests and are separate charges: explain that with the request ids and times, then follow the policy row for a duplicate the console does not confirm.
   - Already credited: a credit note exists on the duplicate; say so, don't credit again.
   - Correct charge the developer wants removed or reduced (goodwill, waiver, SLA/service credit, exception, retries, refund): Support explains why it is billed and routes the request per policy; it issues nothing.
   - Wrong rate, quantity or unexplained amount: route per policy with the evidence.
5. For a confirmed duplicate, check Support's authority for this account in the current authority page (which plans/contract status Support may credit) and the limit for this invoice in Finance's current matrix. Limits can differ by price book or period: work out which applies to this invoice (follow the page the matrix cites, e.g. a close calendar). Drafts, proposals and Slack don't count.
   - Support may credit and the copy line is within the limit: `confirm_with_developer` ("credit note of $X for the duplicated line L on invoice I"), then `issue_credit_note` for the full amount of the copy line with reason `duplicate`, citing `policy_source` and the applicable `policy_limit`.
   - Over the limit, or an account Support may not credit: don't credit. Confirm, `open_dispute` on the copy line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with its request ids), then `escalate_case` to the team policy names with the invoice, both line ids, the dispute id and the window in the account's billing timezone.
6. Routing without a write: load the `billing-handoff` skill.
7. Reply: what the console shows (lines, request ids, amounts), what you did (credit note id and amount, or dispute/case and team), and what happens next per policy (e.g. when a credit is applied). Don't promise outcomes, refund timing or amounts the policy doesn't state."}

{"query": "Support Console duplicate-charge credit authority limit Finance Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix current duplicate charge row Support may credit plans", "results": [{"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-05", "text": "| Situation | What Support does |
|---|---|
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line within Support's limit | Issue one credit note with reason `duplicate` for the full amount of the duplicated line, against that line. No handoff is needed. Tell the customer the amount credited. |
| Confirmed duplicate, duplicated line over the limit | Don't credit. Open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. |
| Duplicate the console doesn't confirm (different request IDs, or no second line) | Don't credit. Collect the intake details and hand the case to Billing Ops as the routing page describes. |
Support's limit is set by Finance in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive) (the duplicate-charge credit row). It is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits."}, {"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-02-26", "text": "meta: author=Dev Patel; owner_team=customer-success; labels=billing, credits, disputes, support-console, support-process, policy-change; created_at=2027-02-24
[body]
## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you."}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-26", "text": "- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason.
## Approval matrix
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Invoices rated on the 2027 price book: up to $250 per duplicated line. Invoices rated on an earlier price book: up to $500 per duplicated line (Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods gives the usage each price book applies to). Over the limit, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |"}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "updated": "2027-02-26", "text": "| Re-issued invoice (address, PO number, tax ID) | Billing Ops | No limit; no change to amounts |
## Evidence each adjustment needs
- **Duplicate-charge credit**: the invoice number, both line IDs and the request IDs they bill. The console confirms the duplicate; a matching description or amount alone is not evidence.
- **Billing-error correction**: the line, the expected rate or quantity and where it comes from (price book, order form).
- **Goodwill and SLA credits**: the customer's ask, the amount if given, and the reason. The account team adds contract references for SLA claims.
- **Write-offs**: collections history and the Controller's note.
## Audit trail
Every adjustment is recorded on the invoice it changes, with the approver's name and the evidence above. Console credit notes record the issuing agent and the reason code automatically. Adjustments issued outside the console are logged by Billing Ops in the adjustments register within one business day."}, {"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-02-26", "text": "The limit is per duplicated line and applies to the line's full amount. Don't split a larger duplicate into several smaller credits.
## What Support never credits
- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.
- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.
## Telling the customer
- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date."}, {"source": "confluence/policies-and-process/delegation-of-authority/support-charter-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Charter 2027: What the Support Agent May and May Not Do", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-03-24", "text": "meta: author=Dev Patel; owner_team=customer-success; created_at=2027-03-20; labels=support-process, billing, authority
[body]
## Purpose
This charter is the source of truth for what the support agent may and may not do. It takes precedence over proposals, drafts, Slack threads, and older pages where they disagree.
## Credits and disputes
- Support can issue duplicate-charge credit notes only on self-serve accounts.
- Support may not issue a credit note of any amount on an account with a signed contract (Enterprise).
- For a confirmed duplicate on a contract account, open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. Billing Ops applies contract-account adjustments under the contract."}, {"source": "confluence/policies-and-process/delegation-of-authority/support-charter-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Charter 2027: What the Support Agent May and May Not Do", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-03-24", "text": "## What does not change
- Everything else in Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2) still applies, as does the billing case routing and handoffs page. Both are linked above.
## What changes Support's authority
- Proposals, drafts and Slack threads don't change Support's authority. Only a published charter revision does.
## Scope
This charter covers the support agent and every human working the support queue, in every channel. Team procedures (credits and disputes, routing, card data) say how to do each thing; this page says whether Support may do it at all.
## Support may
- Look up a customer's billing account, invoices, usage and credits in the console, and answer from them.
- Explain billing behaviour from the published pages.
- Issue a duplicate-charge credit note on a self-serve account, within the limit Finance sets.
- Open a dispute on a duplicated line.
- Open a case with the team the routing page names, and tell the customer who has it."}, {"source": "confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/marketplace-credit-memo-limits-2027", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Marketplace Credit Memos: Approval Limits (2027)", "status": "published", "updated": "2027-02-04", "text": "meta: author=Rishi Malhotra; owner_team=finance-legal; created_at=2027-02-01; labels=marketplace, credits, approvals
[body]
## Scope
Credit memos that Partnerships raises through the AWS or GCP marketplace for marketplace-billed customers. They are not Support console credit notes, and they don't apply to direct Redwood invoices; Support's own limit is in the Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix.
## Limits
- Up to $1,000 per memo: Partnerships.
- Above $1,000: FP&A.
_Last reviewed 2027-02-04._"}]}

{"name": "billing-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed. Search the routing policy (`search_knowledge`, e.g. "billing case routing <topic>"). If a current page explains what the developer sees, or they only asked a question (how something is billed, what their contract says, typical amounts), answer it and stop: no case. Open a case only when they ask for something Support can't do in the conversation, or report a problem the pages don't explain.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing passage for this exact situation. Watch for the distinguishing condition in each row: billing channel (direct vs marketplace/reseller), plan (self-serve vs contract), whether the charge is an error or correct, whether the console confirms the problem. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (e.g. a contract), follow the policy row for that.
3. Collect the intake that row lists. Use what the developer already wrote and the console; call `ask_developer` once for the rest (e.g. invoice_id, line_items, request_ids, time_of_issue + timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract). Give time windows in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account) as well as UTC. If they don't have something, proceed and record it as missing.
4. Answer everything you can first: escalation closes the console for the rest of the conversation.
5. A handoff with no credit note or dispute needs no confirmation. If the handoff includes a dispute, get an explicit yes for the dispute first. If the developer declined the action, open no case.
6. `escalate_case` once: team, priority (normal unless the current routing policy says urgent for this case), a summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what policy says, what you already did), details (account_id, invoice_id, line_ids, request_ids, amounts, window, error code, plan/contract, missing items, policy source ids), and the dispute id if any. Never put card numbers in a case.
7. Tell the developer the team that has it, the case id, what that team does next per policy, and that you can't promise an outcome, amount or date."}

## Scope
Customers who buy Redwood through a reseller receive the reseller's invoice, not Redwood's. This page covers disputes and credits on those invoices only. It is not the procedure for duplicate charges on a direct Redwood invoice; for those, use the support console credits and disputes page.
## What Support does
- Confirm in the console that the account is reseller-billed. A direct Redwood invoice in the console means this page does not apply.
- Point the customer to their reseller, who raises the dispute with Partnerships.
- Support issues no credit note and opens no dispute for a reseller-billed account: the reseller's invoice isn't in the console.
## Partnerships limits

arguments.summary: Developer requests a credit for a suspected duplicate Embeddings line on the August 2026 direct Redwood invoice. Console confirms L3 is a $340.00 copy of L2 for request req_e55. The published procedure allows Support to credit only within Finance's per-line limit, but no authoritative limit effective for this invoice date could be established from sources current as of Sep 15, 2026; no credit or dispute has been issued.

details.amounts: Duplicate copy line amount $340.00 USD; invoice total $2800.00 USD
details.plan_contract: Hosted Self-Serve; direct billing; no signed contract
details.customer_request: Credit duplicate Embeddings line; customer cites prior support guidance that duplicates had to go through Finance
details.evidence: Invoice console confirms duplicate: L2 original, L3 copy, shared request id req_e55. No credit note exists.
details.policy_sources: confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes (published, 2026-02-05): credit confirmed duplicate only within Finance per-line limit; over-limit duplicates disputed and handed to Billing Ops. confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/billing-case-routing-and-handoffs (published, 2027-03-20): duplicated line on direct Redwood invoice routes to Billing Ops.
details.missing: Authoritative Finance duplicate-credit limit effective for August 2026 usage/invoice was not available; future 2027 matrix cannot establish the applicable 2026 limit. No dispute id; dispute not opened because applicable limit is unknown and customer has not authorized a dispute.

transcript.content:
The invoice does show a confirmed duplicate: **L3 is the $340.00 copy** of L2 for request `req_e55`. The duplicate-credit policy allows Support to credit within Finance’s per-line limit, but I couldn’t verify the limit that applies to this August 2026 invoice, so I haven’t issued a credit or opened a dispute.

I’ve sent it to **Billing Ops** for review under case **CASE-1**. Your earlier guidance that duplicates always have to go through Finance doesn’t match the published procedure I found; whether Support can credit this line depends on the applicable limit. Billing Ops will review the duplicate and the limit; I can’t promise an outcome or date.
